files.content:
# Todo List Service: Minimum Requirements Analysis

## Introduction
A Todo list backend service enables users to manage simple tasks. This minimum-version specification defines the essential business requirements and behavioral expectations for a robust, single-user Todo list application, including authentication and comprehensive error handling. The service prioritizes clarity, predictability, and highest usability for its core features.

---

## User Actors and Permissions
| Actor  | Description                                 |
|--------|---------------------------------------------|
| user   | Any authenticated individual managing their personal todo list |
| admin  | (Optional for audit and debugging; not required for minimum functionality) |

- WHEN unauthenticated, users SHALL NOT access any Todo list functionality.
- WHEN authenticated, users SHALL ONLY access, modify, or delete their own Todo items.
- IF admin actor exists, THEN admin SHALL be able to audit but NOT alter or delete user todos directly.

---

## Minimal Functional Requirements (EARS Format)
### Todo Item Management
- WHEN a user is authenticated, THE system SHALL allow creating a new todo item with a required text description and optional completion flag (default: incomplete).
- WHEN a user creates a todo with empty or blank description, THE system SHALL reject the creation with INPUT_400 error and message "Todo description must not be empty."
- WHEN a user creates a todo with description exceeding the system-defined limit (e.g., 256 characters), THE system SHALL reject the request with INPUT_400 error and specify the maximum length allowed.
- WHEN a user lists todos, THE system SHALL return all their own todo items sorted by creation time, newest first.
- WHEN a user updates a todo description, THE system SHALL validate presence and length as per above rules, and SHALL update only if the todo belongs to the user.
- WHEN a user marks a todo as complete or incomplete, THE system SHALL update the corresponding status only if the todo belongs to the user.
- WHEN a user deletes a todo, THE system SHALL delete only if the todo belongs to them, and deleting completed todos SHALL be allowed and idempotent.

### Error Handling and Business Rule Enforcement
Based on robust error handling strategy:
- WHEN a user provides incorrect input (missing fields, description too long, non-existent todo id), THE system SHALL respond with INPUT_400 or NOTFOUND_404 error and a clear, actionable message.
- WHEN an action is attempted on another user's todo id, THE system SHALL return AUTH_403 "Forbidden" error and SHALL NOT reveal whether such a todo exists.
- WHEN requests exceed quota (optional daily creation limit), THE system SHALL respond with LIMIT_429 and guidance when the user may retry.
- WHEN technical issues arise, THE system SHALL return a SERVER_500 error with non-technical user feedback and SHALL not expose system internals.

### Idempotency and Resource State
- WHEN an operation is repeated (e.g., marking already completed todo as complete), THE system SHALL treat the operation idempotently and return updated status without error.

### Success Criteria for Functional Requirements
- All workflows SHALL be covered by automated tests derived from these requirements.

---

## Authentication, Authorization, and Session Management
- WHEN a request is received for any Todo list API, THE system SHALL require the user to authenticate using industry standard methods (e.g., password, OAuth, etc.).
- WHEN authentication fails or session expires, THE system SHALL return AUTH_401 and SHALL NOT disclose user existence or system details.
- WHEN logged in, each user SHALL only access, update, complete, or delete their own todos, never those of others.

---

## User Scenarios & Workflows
### Standard Todo CRUD
- WHEN authenticated, users SHALL be able to:
  - Create: Add a todo item with a short textual description.
  - Read: Retrieve a list of all their todo items, newest first, including completion state.
  - Update: Edit the description or completion status of their own todos.
  - Delete: Remove their own todo items.

### Error and Edge Case Scenarios
- WHEN a user sends a request with incomplete or malformed data, THE system SHALL return an INPUT_400 error specifying which input is incorrect.
- WHEN a user attempts to delete or update a todo they do not own, THE system SHALL return AUTH_403 error.
- WHEN a request uses an expired or invalid authentication token, THE system SHALL return AUTH_401 error and require the user to re-authenticate.
- WHEN system experiences a transient error (e.g., database unavailable), THE system SHALL retry where safe, log the issue, and return SERVER_500 if unsuccessful.
- WHEN the same create, complete, or delete operation is repeated, THE system SHALL act idempotently.

---

## Input and Output Validation
- WHEN any field is required by business rules, THE system SHALL validate its presence and enforce minimum/maximum length where appropriate.
- WHEN optional fields are omitted, THE system SHALL supply sensible defaults (e.g., incomplete status for new todos).
- WHEN invalid or extra fields are supplied, THE system SHALL ignore extras and validate essentials only.

---

## Error Handling: Codes and Principles
- Error response to users SHALL include:
  - HTTP error class (e.g., 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 500)
  - Error code (AUTH_401, AUTH_403, INPUT_400, NOTFOUND_404, LIMIT_429, SERVER_500, etc.)
  - Clear, actionable human-friendly message
  - Optional validation hints for input corrections

### Error Handling Workflow (Mermaid Diagram)
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Submits Request"] --> B{"Request Valid?"}
  B -->|"Yes"| C["Perform Business Logic"]
  B -->|"No"| D["Return INPUT_400 with field-specific errors"]
  C --> E{"Business Rule Violation?"}
  E -->|"No"| F["Commit Operation and Return Success"]
  E -->|"Yes"| G["Return Business Rule Error (e.g., LIMIT_429)"]
  F --> H["End"]
  D --> H
  G --> H
  C --> I{"System Error?"}
  I -->|"No"| F
  I -->|"Yes"| J["Return SERVER_500 and Log Details"]
  J --> H
```
---

## Non-Functional Requirements
- THE system SHALL respond to user requests within 1 second under normal load.
- THE system SHALL be available 99.9% of the time (excluding planned maintenance).
- THE system SHALL never expose implementation details, stack traces, or sensitive data in any user-facing message.
- ALL processes SHALL be atomic where possible, ensuring users never see partial changes.
- ALL error conditions SHALL be covered by test cases and logged internally for system monitoring and debugging.

---

## Conclusion
- This specification is sufficient for backend engineers to implement a minimal, production-grade Todo list backend service with industry-standard reliability and user-centric error handling, meeting all key business requirements without ambiguity.

models.name: todo_list_system_settings
models.description:
Global system settings and platform-wide configuration parameters.

This table stores platform-level flags, operational options, or dynamic infrastructure configuration values that affect the overall behavior of the Todo List service. It allows the backend to flexibly enable, disable, or adjust global features without redeployment. Each record represents a uniquely identified setting (by key), with support for versioned values, clear description, and retrieval metadata.

This is the authoritative source for all service-wide configuration values. There are no foreign keys; all relationships are internal to this domain component. Optimized for rapid lookup and extensibility.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique setting identifier. This field acts as a business-meaningful key for the configuration parameter (e.g., 'max_login_attempts', 'enable_signup'). Maximum length: 100 characters. Index enforced.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Setting value as a string. Used to store dynamic configuration values in string format. Up to 1024 characters. Application responsible for type-casting on retrieval.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the setting. Used for documenting the business context, operational semantics, or instructions for each platform option. Optional, for service administrator reference.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when the setting was first created. Set by the backend upon insertion (ISO 8601 format, UTC).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this setting. Managed by the backend (ISO 8601 format, UTC).

models.name: todo_list_users
models.description:
Registered end users of the Todo List system.

Represents any individual who can register, authenticate, and manage their personal set of todo items. Each user is identified by a unique email and secures access with a hashed password. Designed for strict privacy and least-privilege access: users may act only on their own data and cannot view or alter other users. Status fields support account locking for abuse or compliance. Auditing is handled via associated session and audit log tables.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for login, identity, and communication for this user. Must be globally unique across all users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt or argon2id hash of user's chosen password. Never store a plain password; always enforce strong hash.

plainFields.name: is_locked
plainFields.description: True if the user account is locked or suspended and should not be allowed to authenticate. Used for abuse prevention and compliance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for the latest account modification or status change.

models.name: todo_list_user_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for end users of the Todo List system.

Each session tracks login context for a specific user, including connection IP and access URL. Sessions are used for token validation, security context, and auditing. Multiple sessions may exist per user, supporting concurrent device access. Expired sessions are tracked for compliance and security analysis. Managed via parent user lifecycle. Only allowed fields per session table standard.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to session-owning user. Links to {@link todo_list_users.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address for the origin of the session, for security auditing.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Original connection URL associated with this session, useful for context and traceability.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL context for original login or session creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp of session authentication creation event.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this session expired (null means still active).

models.name: todo_list_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts for privileged operations and oversight in the Todo List service.

Admins have the ability to view, edit, and manage any user's todos as well as oversee user accounts and system health. Each admin is identified by a unique email and secures access via a hashed password field. Admin accounts are strictly separated from regular users for security and compliance. Includes lock flag for suspensions and audit triggers. Admin capabilities are managed exclusively by the RBAC patterns of the application; they do not have their own todo entries.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Globally unique admin login address for identity and communication.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Strong cryptographic hash of admin password for login authentication. Plain password never stored.

plainFields.name: is_locked
plainFields.description: True if admin is suspended or access is temporarily revoked. Used for security and compliance enforcement.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for admin account creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for last update to the admin account.

models.name: todo_list_admin_sessions
models.description:
Authentication session records for administrators in the Todo List system.

Each session logs admin login context, including IP and URL reference chains, for auditing privileged system access. Supports concurrent sessions per admin (for monitoring concurrent workstations or incident response). Expired sessions are kept for compliance and future security analysis. Follows the session table standard for admins as a distinct actor class. Managed through the parent admin lifecycle only.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to session-owning admin. Links to {@link todo_list_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address where admin logged in to begin session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Target URL of session origin, useful for context and audit trail.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Upstream URL from which admin accessed this session. Used in audit trails.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp of session authentication creation.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: UTC time session expired; null for active session.

models.name: todo_list_todos
models.description:
Main table for user-owned todo items following strict ownership policy.

Defines individual todos with required description, completion status, timestamps, and ownership linked directly to the user. Enforces business rules for CRUD, soft/hard delete, and status toggling. Supports API filtering by completion and deleted state. Titles and descriptions are validated for length, content, and duplication. Each todo is owned by exactly one user and cannot be accessed or modified by others except admins via compliance interfaces. Soft delete logic enforces 2-minute undo for user deletions, immediate permanent deletion by admins. Temporal fields track creation, last update, soft deletion, and completion timestamps. Only users may create todos; admins cannot own personal tasks.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each todo item.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the owning user. Associates todo with exactly one user. {@link todo_list_users.id}.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Todo task description, maximum 255 characters. Cannot be empty or whitespace only. Must be unique for user within duplicate suppression interval.

plainFields.name: completed
plainFields.description: Completion state of the todo. True if completed, false if incomplete.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for when the todo was marked as complete, in UTC. Null if incomplete.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was created, in UTC ISO 8601 format.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was last updated (description or completed status).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for when the todo was soft-deleted (for undo window); null if not deleted or after hard deletion.

models.name: todo_list_todo_audit_logs
models.description:
Audit trail for all privileged or destructive operations on todos, supporting compliance, traceability, and support review.

Records all user and admin actions affecting todo items, including CRUD operations, status changes, and admin interventions. Logs actor context (user or admin), action type, timestamps, affected todo item, and reason or context messages. This table is append-only; records are immutable and never deleted. Used exclusively for compliance, security, and recovery audits; not directly visible to end users. Supports queries by actor, action, time, and affected todo for post-incident or operational review. Ensures historical accountability for all todo lifecycle events.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique audit log entry identifier.

foreignFields.name: todo_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the affected todo item. {@link todo_list_todos.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the acting user involved in the audited operation, if applicable. Nullable if action was performed only by an admin. {@link todo_list_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the acting admin if the operation was performed by an administrator. Nullable if actor was a regular user. {@link todo_list_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Action type: created, updated, completed, uncompleted, deleted, restored, admin_deleted, admin_edited. Fixed set for audit granularity.

plainFields.name: context
plainFields.description: Optional audit details: inputs, reason, API source, context message, etc. Allows traceability and user support in incident review.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for when the audit log entry was created, in UTC ISO 8601 format.

### `todo_list_system_settings`

Global system settings and platform-wide configuration parameters.

This table stores platform-level flags, operational options, or dynamic
infrastructure configuration values that affect the overall behavior of
the Todo List service. It allows the backend to flexibly enable, disable,
or adjust global features without redeployment. Each record represents a
uniquely identified setting (by key), with support for versioned values,
clear description, and retrieval metadata.

This is the authoritative source for all service-wide configuration
values. There are no foreign keys; all relationships are internal to this
domain component. Optimized for rapid lookup and extensibility.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `key`
  > Unique setting identifier. This field acts as a business-meaningful key
  > for the configuration parameter (e.g., 'max_login_attempts',
  > 'enable_signup'). Maximum length: 100 characters. Index enforced.
- `value`
  > Setting value as a string. Used to store dynamic configuration values in
  > string format. Up to 1024 characters. Application responsible for
  > type-casting on retrieval.
- `description`
  > Detailed description of the setting. Used for documenting the business
  > context, operational semantics, or instructions for each platform option.
  > Optional, for service administrator reference.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp indicating when the setting was first created. Set by the
  > backend upon insertion (ISO 8601 format, UTC).
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of the most recent update to this setting. Managed by the
  > backend (ISO 8601 format, UTC).

### `todo_list_users`

Registered end users of the Todo List system.

Represents any individual who can register, authenticate, and manage
their personal set of todo items. Each user is identified by a unique
email and secures access with a hashed password. Designed for strict
privacy and least-privilege access: users may act only on their own data
and cannot view or alter other users. Status fields support account
locking for abuse or compliance. Auditing is handled via associated
session and audit log tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address for login, identity, and communication for this
  > user. Must be globally unique across all users.
- `password_hash`
  > Bcrypt or argon2id hash of user's chosen password. Never store a plain
  > password; always enforce strong hash.
- `is_locked`
  > True if the user account is locked or suspended and should not be allowed
  > to authenticate. Used for abuse prevention and compliance.
- `created_at`: UTC timestamp when the user account was created.
- `updated_at`: UTC timestamp for the latest account modification or status change.

### `todo_list_user_sessions`

Authentication sessions for end users of the Todo List system.

Each session tracks login context for a specific user, including
connection IP and access URL. Sessions are used for token validation,
security context, and auditing. Multiple sessions may exist per user,
supporting concurrent device access. Expired sessions are tracked for
compliance and security analysis. Managed via parent user lifecycle. Only
allowed fields per session table standard.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_list_user_id`: Foreign key to session-owning user. Links to [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users).
- `ip`: IP address for the origin of the session, for security auditing.
- `href`
  > Original connection URL associated with this session, useful for context
  > and traceability.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL context for original login or session creation.
- `created_at`: UTC timestamp of session authentication creation event.
- `expired_at`: UTC timestamp when this session expired (null means still active).

### `todo_list_admins`

Administrator accounts for privileged operations and oversight in the
Todo List service.

Admins have the ability to view, edit, and manage any user's todos as
well as oversee user accounts and system health. Each admin is identified
by a unique email and secures access via a hashed password field. Admin
accounts are strictly separated from regular users for security and
compliance. Includes lock flag for suspensions and audit triggers. Admin
capabilities are managed exclusively by the RBAC patterns of the
application; they do not have their own todo entries.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`: Globally unique admin login address for identity and communication.
- `password_hash`
  > Strong cryptographic hash of admin password for login authentication.
  > Plain password never stored.
- `is_locked`
  > True if admin is suspended or access is temporarily revoked. Used for
  > security and compliance enforcement.
- `created_at`: UTC timestamp for admin account creation.
- `updated_at`: UTC timestamp for last update to the admin account.

### `todo_list_admin_sessions`

Authentication session records for administrators in the Todo List system.

Each session logs admin login context, including IP and URL reference
chains, for auditing privileged system access. Supports concurrent
sessions per admin (for monitoring concurrent workstations or incident
response). Expired sessions are kept for compliance and future security
analysis. Follows the session table standard for admins as a distinct
actor class. Managed through the parent admin lifecycle only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_list_admin_id`: Foreign key to session-owning admin. Links to [todo_list_admins.id](#todo_list_admins).
- `ip`: IP address where admin logged in to begin session.
- `href`: Target URL of session origin, useful for context and audit trail.
- `referrer`: Upstream URL from which admin accessed this session. Used in audit trails.
- `created_at`: UTC timestamp of session authentication creation.
- `expired_at`: UTC time session expired; null for active session.

### `todo_list_todos`

Main table for user-owned todo items following strict ownership policy.

Defines individual todos with required description, completion status,
timestamps, and ownership linked directly to the user. Enforces business
rules for CRUD, soft/hard delete, and status toggling. Supports API
filtering by completion and deleted state. Titles and descriptions are
validated for length, content, and duplication. Each todo is owned by
exactly one user and cannot be accessed or modified by others except
admins via compliance interfaces. Soft delete logic enforces 2-minute
undo for user deletions, immediate permanent deletion by admins. Temporal
fields track creation, last update, soft deletion, and completion
timestamps. Only users may create todos; admins cannot own personal
tasks.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each todo item.
- `user_id`
  > Foreign key referencing the owning user. Associates todo with exactly one
  > user. [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users).
- `description`
  > Todo task description, maximum 255 characters. Cannot be empty or
  > whitespace only. Must be unique for user within duplicate suppression
  > interval.
- `completed`: Completion state of the todo. True if completed, false if incomplete.
- `completed_at`
  > Timestamp for when the todo was marked as complete, in UTC. Null if
  > incomplete.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the todo was created, in UTC ISO 8601 format.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was last updated (description or completed
  > status).
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp for when the todo was soft-deleted (for undo window); null if
  > not deleted or after hard deletion.

### `todo_list_todo_audit_logs`

Audit trail for all privileged or destructive operations on todos,
supporting compliance, traceability, and support review.

Records all user and admin actions affecting todo items, including CRUD
operations, status changes, and admin interventions. Logs actor context
(user or admin), action type, timestamps, affected todo item, and reason
or context messages. This table is append-only; records are immutable and
never deleted. Used exclusively for compliance, security, and recovery
audits; not directly visible to end users. Supports queries by actor,
action, time, and affected todo for post-incident or operational review.
Ensures historical accountability for all todo lifecycle events.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique audit log entry identifier.
- `todo_id`
  > Foreign key referencing the affected todo item. {@link
  > todo_list_todos.id}.
- `actor_user_id`
  > Foreign key to the acting user involved in the audited operation, if
  > applicable. Nullable if action was performed only by an admin. {@link
  > todo_list_users.id}.
- `actor_admin_id`
  > Foreign key to the acting admin if the operation was performed by an
  > administrator. Nullable if actor was a regular user. {@link
  > todo_list_admins.id}.
- `action`
  > Action type: created, updated, completed, uncompleted, deleted, restored,
  > admin_deleted, admin_edited. Fixed set for audit granularity.
- `context`
  > Optional audit details: inputs, reason, API source, context message, etc.
  > Allows traceability and user support in incident review.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp for when the audit log entry was created, in UTC ISO 8601
  > format.

operations.specification: Implements user registration for the Todo List system, writing a new user account to the todo_list_users table and securely hashing the user's password. Ensures the email address provided is globally unique and immediately returns a JWT token set (access/refresh) with encoded user ID, role, and permissions. Required schema fields for account creation—email and password_hash—are stored, with additional metadata for account status and auditing. Enforces least-privilege access: each user can only access their own data. Password management and security requirements are met via password_hash and uniqueness constraints. If an email is already registered or invalid, the operation fails gracefully.
operations.description:
This operation provides the mechanism for user registration within the Todo List system.

It accepts a user's email address and password, validates that the provided email is unique (as enforced by the unique constraint on the email field in the todo_list_users table), and securely stores a hash of the user's password in the password_hash column. No plain-text passwords are ever stored; all password security requirements are dictated by strong hashing as noted in the schema's password_hash comment.

Upon successful creation of the user account, the system issues a signed JWT containing the new user's id (from todo_list_users.id), role, and associated permissions determined by their registration as a user. Session information is also established for auditing and session expiry (linked through peripheral tables).

Security is managed through unique email enforcement, proper hashing, status checks on is_locked (to immediately lock any account if necessary), and audit-compliant timestamp fields created_at and updated_at. The account remains locked if system rules require it (e.g., for compliance or abuse).

This endpoint is the entry point for all new user onboarding and triggers follow-up flows like login, password reset, or account management. All expected errors (duplicate email, hashing failure, invalid input) return clear, safe messages. Related endpoints: login, refresh, or user password reset.
operations.summary: Register a new user in todo_list_users with email and hashed password, returning JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: New user registration payload including required email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorized user result with JWT tokens, role, and user data.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implements secure authentication for existing Todo List users using credentials checked against todo_list_users (email, password_hash). Verifies that the user exists, the provided password matches the securely stored hash, and the account is not locked (checked via is_locked column). On successful login: issues new JWT (access + refresh) token pair with embedded permissions and session meta-data. Logs all unsuccessful login attempts per schema comments and securely rejects invalid/expired credentials. Integrates with session management to enforce login attempt throttling or lockout if system policies require. Only allows users whose is_locked is false to successfully authenticate.
operations.description:
This operation implements user login to the Todo List system.

It cross-checks provided credentials (email and password) with the corresponding user's email and password_hash stored in the todo_list_users Prisma model. Successful validation requires matching email, valid password (after hash check), and that is_locked is false (account is not currently suspended or disabled).

Upon successful authentication, the system issues a freshly signed JWT containing the user's id, permissions, and an expiration timestamp derived from project-wide session policy. Timestamps in created_at and updated_at support session and compliance audits.

All failed authentication attempts are securely logged, and if required by business rules, may increment a failure counter and/or trigger lockout (via is_locked) if abuse/threats detected. If the user is locked, authentication fails gracefully with a clear error.

This endpoint works in concert with user registration, refresh token, and password reset flows. It does not reveal the existence of locked or unregistered accounts in its error responses, minimizing security risk.
operations.summary: Authenticate existing user in todo_list_users, issue JWT upon valid credentials and account status.

requestBody.description: User login credentials: email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorized user result with issued JWT tokens and user permissions.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Issues new authentication tokens for an existing, valid Todo List user session by verifying provided refresh token and generating new JWT tokens referencing the user in the todo_list_users table. Ensures the user account is still valid (not locked or deleted) and maintains original permissions/role context. Uses standard JWT expiry/rotation mechanisms as described in requirements. All schema-driven fields—user id, email, is_locked—are used in vetting the session before refreshing. If the user account is locked, expired, or otherwise invalidated, token refresh fails gracefully with proper errors.
operations.description:
This operation provides JWT token refresh for authenticated users in the Todo List system.

It accepts a valid refresh token (previously issued through login or join) and validates the associated user by confirming presence and status (using todo_list_users.id, email, is_locked fields). Only users whose is_locked is false receive new tokens. The rotation of access/refresh tokens strictly follows the requirements, including max life, security, and auditing through timestamps (created_at/updated_at).

If the session is valid, this operation issues new JWT tokens (access/refresh) embedding the correct user permissions, id, and expiry policy as mandated by the schema and system session management policies. If the session is invalid—account locked, token expired or not found—an appropriate error is returned.

Token refresh is crucial for session continuity without requiring frequent re-logins, while preserving security by enforcing short access lifetime and auditability. Works closely with registration and login endpoints.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT tokens for valid sessions on todo_list_users, revalidating permissions and account status.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for JWT renewal flow.

responseBody.description: Authorized user result with renewed JWT tokens and user context.

It accepts administrator registration data, specifically email and password (hashed). Upon successfully creating the account, it returns an authorized session with a JWT for authenticated access. Operation ensures unique email constraint and secures the password via cryptographic hash storage only (password_hash). Access is public, intended for new admin registration, and is typically restricted or audited in practice.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables the registration of a new administrator.

The core operation corresponds to the 'todo_list_admins' Prisma schema, utilizing the 'email' field (globally unique) and a strong 'password_hash' for secret management. New administrator accounts must be immediately associated with required user metadata ('created_at', 'updated_at'), maintaining compliance and audit granularity.

On registration, the password is never stored directly; only the securely hashed 'password_hash' is populated. The endpoint follows strict validation logic to ensure both the uniqueness of the email (enforced at the schema and API layers) and password policy compliance.

Successful registration initiates a first authentication session (see: 'todo_list_admin_sessions') and issues JWT tokens for subsequent admin requests. The account's 'is_locked' property is always set to 'false' at creation for initial access unless overridden by compliance/triggers.

For onboarding flows, consider integrating this operation with an external approval or notification workflow. Related operations: 'login', 'refresh'.

It issues JWT tokens for successful authentication. Checks that the account is not locked (is_locked = false), and that both email and password_hash match. Logs a new session in the 'todo_list_admin_sessions' table for auditing. Fails authentication if credentials are invalid or the admin is locked. Publicly accessible for credentialed users.

The login API enables administrators to obtain access credentials after verifying their identity.

Upon success, a new session record is created in 'todo_list_admin_sessions', associating login metadata such as IP address and user agent for audit tracking.

Authentication tokens (JWT) are returned as part of the response, following RBAC best practices. Account lockouts and repeated failed attempts are to be handled by an external security process if not described in this schema.

Follows session revocation and replacement rules, and updates session expiration for auditing and compliance.
operations.description:
The refresh endpoint enables administrators to renew their authentication tokens without resubmitting credentials.

Works with the 'todo_list_admin_sessions' Prisma model: the request must include a valid, unexpired refresh token that links to an existing session (fields: 'created_at', 'expired_at').

Additional checks verify the associated admin in 'todo_list_admins' is still active (not 'is_locked'), guaranteeing only authorized, eligible admins may refresh their sessions.

Success results in new tokens and session lifespan extension, while invalid, expired, or revoked sessions are rejected for security compliance. Token rotation and audit events should be managed as described by system security policies.

Frequently used together with 'login' and 'join' operations; follow best practices to limit session duration and enforce single-device or multi-session limits as needed by business logic.

It is associated with the todo_list_todos table, which defines the structure and business rules for user-owned todo items. The operation ensures strict ownership enforcement—only the owner or administrators may access the todo, with all access and error conditions reflecting both completion and deletion state. The operation returns a fully detailed todo object including all descriptive and status fields. If the todo is not found or the requester lacks permission, the API returns an appropriate error.

All fields—including description, completed state, completed_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at—are returned, reflecting the most up-to-date status of the todo. Access is strictly enforced: the todo can only be retrieved if the requester is either the owner or is accessing it through admin compliance functions.

Requests for non-existent or inaccessible todos result in a suitable error response, ensuring compliance with business rules on privacy and data access. This operation fully aligns with the requirements of the todo_list_todos table and its detailed comments on ownership and temporal fields.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item, recorded in the todo_list_todos table. The endpoint is designed for end users to add personal task items with strict ownership enforcement: the created todo is associated with exactly one user and cannot be owned by an administrator. The operation validates all required fields, including the non-empty description (max 255 characters), initial completion state, and default timestamps. Duplicate descriptions for a user within a suppression interval are prevented by unique constraints. Only authenticated users may create todos, with all required metadata managed automatically by the system. Success returns the full details of the created todo item, including new timestamps and status.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item in the user-owned todo list system. The requester must be an authenticated user; administrators are not allowed to own todos.

Input fields are validated per the database schema, with the description required, a maximum of 255 characters, and duplicate prevention within a unique constraint period. Timestamps for creation and update are set automatically; completion and deletion state are tracked. The created todo is fully owned by the requesting user, with no cross-user access allowed. If constraints are violated, an error response is returned.

This operation strictly follows the business logic specified for the todo_list_todos table, ensuring personal ownership, compliance with system rules, and immediate reflection of the created todo's state.
operations.summary: Create a new todo item for the authenticated user in todo_list_todos.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo item with all fields populated.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo item in the system. It operates on the todo_list_todos table and allows users to modify the description, completion status, or other updatable fields of their personal todo. The operation strictly enforces ownership: only the user who owns the todo or an administrator can update it. Business rules from the schema are honored, ensuring the description remains unique for the user (within the duplicate suppression interval) and meets all validation constraints (non-empty, maximum 255 characters). When the completion status is changed, the completed_at field updates accordingly. All updates automatically refresh the updated_at timestamp. Soft-deleted todos cannot be updated by users, but may be recovered or permanently altered by admins in compliance scenarios. Access is denied to unauthorized users or if the todo has been hard deleted. The operation leverages the primary key id as the path parameter, formatted as a UUID.
operations.description:
Update the fields of an existing todo item such as its description or completed state. Only the user who owns the todo may update it, enforcing strict ownership policy mandated in the database schema and business requirements.

When successful, this operation ensures all content and validation rules are met, including unique descriptions for the user (with regard to timing of duplicate submissions) and conformity to length and content checks. If the status is marked as complete, the completed_at field is set to the current UTC timestamp; if reverted to incomplete, completed_at is cleared. Record's updated_at is refreshed on any modification.

Soft-deleted todos are locked from user updates but may be administered by privileged roles for compliance actions. Unauthorized attempts yield appropriate error messages including permission denied or not found. The response returns the updated todo object for client synchronization. This API endpoint requires the user be authenticated, and administrators have elevated access for managing any user's todos as required by compliance rules.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently erases (hard deletes) a todo item from the system. It executes on the todo_list_todos table using the id as the identifier parameter. Only the owner of the todo or an administrator may erase the item. When a todo is deleted by a user, the system typically applies a soft-delete policy with a 2-minute undo window, as tracked by the deleted_at timestamp. However, this specific operation performs a hard delete—removing the record entirely and bypassing the soft-delete protection. This capability is reserved mainly for administrators handling compliance or data hygiene operations; users should use the standard deletion endpoint for undo-capable removal.

The operation validates the caller's ownership or administrative privilege before erasure. Associated business invariants and secondary effects—such as removal from the user's active todo list—are enforced. Once erased, the todo is no longer restorable or visible via any API endpoint. Reference integrity is ensured.

Path parameter is the primary UUID key of the todo_list_todos table. This operation is fully audited and limited to avoid unintended permanent data loss.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a todo item from the database. This operation is intended mainly for compliance or administrative enforcement, as regular user removal typically employs soft-deletion with undo capability by setting deleted_at and not erasing data immediately.

Strict permission checks are applied: only the owning user and administrators may invoke this hard delete. Once successful, the todo is purged from all lists and cannot be recovered. Attempts to erase already-removed or non-existent todos yield an appropriate error. The erasure is fully audited for compliance.

Field-level validation and referential integrity are enforced by business rules in the system schema. This endpoint should be reserved for privileged actors. Normal users should be encouraged to use soft-delete endpoints unless compliance requires hard erasure.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of audit log entries (todo_list_todo_audit_logs) associated with a specific todo item (todo_list_todos). The operation supports querying audit logs by actor (user/admin), action type, and timestamp, providing compliance and traceability for privileged or destructive actions on the todo. It leverages the database schema for flexible search and sorting but is strictly tied to one todo per invocation using the todo's unique identifier. Only administrative users can run this query for compliance or support investigations, as audit logs are never exposed to end users. The results are returned in a paginated summary format suitable for operational review.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of audit trail records for a specific todo item. This endpoint provides advanced search capabilities on audit logs linked to the target todo, supporting filtering by actor (user/admin), action, and time range.

Audit logs track all privileged or destructive modifications—including CRUD operations, status changes, admin interventions, and manual deletions—across the todo's lifecycle. Each log entry provides full actor context and an immutable record of who, what, and when, supporting compliance with historical traceability requirements.

Only admin users can access this endpoint, as regular users and even todo creators may not review audit logs. The API response structure conforms to `IPageITodoListTodoAuditLog.ISummary` for compatibility with compliance dashboards, audit reviews, and operational forensics tools. Related endpoints include detail retrieval for a single audit log entry.

responseBody.description: Paginated summary of audit log entries for the given todo item, matching search criteria.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Audit logs are always linked to a specific todo item. The todo must exist before audit logs can be created or queried, so POST /todoList/user/todos is required to establish the todo context for audit logs.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the detailed information of a specific audit log entry (todo_list_todo_audit_logs) by its unique identifier, scoped under the context of a given todo item (todo_list_todos). It is used by administrators for compliance audit, incident forensics, and support review purposes. The endpoint enforces strict admin-only access due to the sensitive nature of audit log data. All actor context, action, timestamps, and optional context messages are returned, providing a comprehensive view of the logged event.
operations.description:
Get detailed information for an individual audit log associated with a given todo item. This endpoint returns all relevant data for a single immutable audit event, including actor user/admin, action type, event context, and exact timestamp.

Audit logs are append-only and cannot be deleted or modified; this guarantees historical accuracy in compliance and audit processes. Admins use this operation to review critical or suspicious actions in-depth or to support retrospective incident investigations.

User access is strictly forbidden for audit details; only administrators holding compliance or operational permissions can utilize this endpoint. The response conforms to the `ITodoListTodoAuditLog` DTO structure and supports integration with compliance tooling and audit dashboards. For list queries, use the collection endpoint for audit logs of a todo.

ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
DTO for Todo List system end-user creation, mapped directly to the persistent database model.

Only the email and plain password fields are required and persisted; all other fields (created_at, updated_at, is_locked, password_hash) are system-managed and not settable by the client. The client must supply a plain password that will be securely hashed by backend logic before storage. The system enforces global uniqueness on the email. Account lock and audit data are managed internally.

email.description: Unique email address for registration and future authentication. Must be globally unique. Used for identity and communication. Case-insensitive. Validated against RFC email format.

password.description: Plain text password supplied by the registering user. Backend will securely hash before storage; client must never provide a hash.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authorization result DTO for Todo List end-user authentication flows (join, login, refresh).

This structure delivers authentication tokens along with all safe-to-expose user context, encapsulated in the 'user' property as a summary of account essentials. The root level holds only authentication/session artifacts ("token") and a current snapshot of user state in 'user' – never duplicate or raw sensitive fields.

Used as the atomic backend result for new user creation, login, or refresh operations. Application code must always display user information exclusively from the nested 'user' summary, treating it as the single source of UI/account context. This separation ensures a DRY and future-proof contract in accordance with backend security requirements and frontend clarity.

See documentation for IAuthorizationToken and ITodoListUser.ISummary for details on tokens and user context.

id.description: User's unique identifier (UUID), assigned at account creation. Used as the primary key in the todo_list_users table.

email.description: User's unique login and contact email, used for communication, identity, and authentication. Must be unique for each user in the system.

is_locked.description: Account lock status. True if the user account is suspended or disabled due to abuse, compliance, or admin action. Locked users cannot login or perform actions.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when the user account was first created in the system.

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp of most recent account update (such as email change or lock status).

user.description: Summary of the authenticated user session. Represents the user's minimal account and status context as sourced directly from the todo_list_users table. Used as the authoritative frontend source for identity/role/sign-in status and system identity.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a registered end user, mapped directly from the todo_list_users table in the Todo List system. This summary variant is used for lists, lightweight user context, and inclusion as a user snapshot in authentication and session DTOs.

Reflects the service's strict privacy controls: never exposes password hashes or internal system fields, and only transmits email, account status, and unique identifier. Auditing and compliance metadata is handled via session and audit tables, not here.

Optimized for both personal and administrative UI listings; suitable for main menu displays, session overlays, and high-trust minimal referencing by other API contracts.

All properties are mapped directly from the primary fields of the todo_list_users schema.

id.description: Unique identifier for the registered user, as sourced from todo_list_users.id. This is a system-generated UUID assigned at registration and serves as the main user reference in all relations.

email.description: Globally unique email address for user authentication and communication. This field is strictly enforced to be unique across the todo_list_users table, and is required for all user-facing operations. Used as the login identity, for notifications, and for account recovery flows.

is_locked.description: Account lock or suspension status as tracked in todo_list_users.is_locked. True indicates the user is currently suspended or disabled due to administrative action or abuse detection; false means active. Determines authentication and access permission in all session flows.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
DTO schema for user login (authentication) in the Todo List system.

This request body is used when a user attempts to authenticate by providing their credentials. It contains the email address (which must be globally unique) and the user's password, which is received as plain text for validation and hashing purposes (never stored as plain text). This DTO does not and must not expose any identity or system fields, matching security-first requirements and business constraints.

Used exclusively in the user login API operation for credential validation and system login. Password is always plain string. All system fields (id, session, status) are derived server-side and never provided by the client. Follows best practice for password handling and authentication flows.

email.description:
End user's globally unique email address for login. This must be provided by the user, and will be checked as the primary identifier in todo_list_users.

Validation: must follow RFC 5322 email format. Example: user@example.com.

password.description: End user's password in plain text form for login authentication. The password will be checked against the stored, securely hashed password in todo_list_users (via password_hash field). Minimum 8 characters. The backend is responsible for hashing and secure verification. Never exposed or stored in plain text beyond this check.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
DTO schema for requesting a refresh of JWT tokens for an authenticated user session in the Todo List system.

This schema is used by the API when a valid refresh token is provided and a new JWT (access & refresh pair) must be issued. The only required property is the refresh token string that was previously issued; all session and user context validation occurs server-side. Never contains system identity or user fields, for strict security and separation of concerns.

refresh_token.description: Opaque refresh token string issued by a previous login or registration operation. Must be provided in full as received. Used to look up and validate existing session. Example: 'eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1N...'. Minimum 32 characters for security.

email.description: Globally unique administrator login email address for access and communication purposes. Must conform to RFC 5322 email format and is validated for uniqueness at the schema and application layers.

password.description: Plain text password used for administrator account registration. Must satisfy system-configured password policy. The password is only accepted here for registration and is never stored in plain form; it is cryptographically hashed and persisted in the password_hash field in the database.

oneOf.description: IP address of the registration requestor for session audit trail, if available (can be IPv4 or IPv6).

ip.description: IP address of the admin registration operation, if available. This field supports both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses or can be null if not captured by the client or server. Used in session context, audit, and security analysis.

href.description: Absolute URL of the page where the registration request originated. Used for session context and audit purposes. Must be a valid absolute URI (RFC 3986). Technically required by session policy.

referrer.description: The referring page URL which led to this admin registration request. Used for audit and session contextualization. Required by security compliance policy and must be a valid absolute URI (can be empty string for direct navigation).

ITodoListAdmin.IJoin.description:
DTO for registering a new administrator account in the Todo List system.

Accepts a unique email (which also serves as the login credential) and a strong password (to be hashed server-side upon creation). Records session context including originating IP address (optional), connection URL (href), and referring URL (referrer).

The password field is for plain text only and must meet system complexity requirements—never stored in the database without hashing. Registration call always attaches creation and update metadata automatically; admin is unlocked at creation. Session-related context used for auditing and compliance.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authorized administrator account registered or authenticated in the Todo List system. Corresponds to the primary key in 'todo_list_admins'.

email.description: Administrator's unique contact email. Used for login and notifications. Must be unique across all admin accounts.

is_locked.description: Indicates whether the admin account is locked and disallowed from performing actions. Used for security suspension and access revocation.

created_at.description: Date and time when the admin account was created, in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the admin account, for audit and compliance purposes.

ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Response DTO representing an authorized administrator session after registration or authentication.

Includes the unique administrator account identifier and issued token(s) to be used as Bearer credentials for access to protected admin endpoints. The token structure adheres to security standards and enables tracking of admin privileges, permissions, and session context.

This type is always returned upon successful registration or login, and may also be issued during token refreshes for ongoing session management.

email.description: Administrator login email address. Must match a registered admin's email from 'todo_list_admins'. Used as unique identifier for privileged login.

password.description: Plain password for authentication. Compared against the stored hash ('password_hash') in 'todo_list_admins'. Must not be empty.

oneOf.description: Login IP address in IPv4 format.
Login IP address in IPv6 format.

ip.description: IP address where admin logged in to begin session. Used for auditing, security monitoring, and session context. Optional; typically extracted by backend if omitted.

href.description: The URL of the page where the login attempt originated. Used for session context and audit trails. Required for new session creation.

referrer.description: The referring URL for the login request. Tracks session chain and audit trails. Required for session creation for compliance.

ITodoListAdmin.ILogin.description:
Request DTO for administrator login in the Todo List service.

Carries admin credentials and session context (connection metadata) for authentication. Email must match an 'todo_list_admins' record; password is compared to stored hash. Provides session audit context through href and referrer fields, with optional explicit IP.

Successful login results in session creation in 'todo_list_admin_sessions'.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token associated with an active admin session, previously issued by the login operation. Must reference a valid, unexpired 'todo_list_admin_sessions' record.

ITodoListAdmin.IRefresh.description:
DTO for refreshing administrator authentication tokens in the Todo List service.

Carries the refresh token issued after a successful login, which must be linked to an active and valid 'todo_list_admin_sessions' record. Used to obtain new access tokens without resubmitting credentials.

Session validity, lock status of the admin, and session expiration are checked as part of refresh. Fails if the session is expired or revoked.

id.description:
Primary key of the system settings record.

Globally unique identifier for each configuration entry, used for precise referencing and lookups at the database layer. Managed by the backend system, not editable by users.

key.description:
Unique setting identifier for system-wide configuration.

This is a business-meaningful symbolic string that identifies a specific global feature, flag, or parameter (for example, 'max_login_attempts', 'enable_signup'). This is the business primary key for platform configuration settings, and must be unique. Indexed for rapid retrieval by key. The system enforces max length 100.

value.description:
Configuration value associated with the given key, stored in string format.

This field encodes the setting's value as a string; application logic is responsible for interpreting as int, boolean, etc. Max length 1024; longer strings will be truncated or rejected.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description for this system setting.

Provides service administrators or platform operators additional context, business meaning, or operational warnings for the configuration parameter. Used for documentation or in management UIs only.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration entry was created.

Set automatically by backend (ISO 8601, UTC). Used for audit/history and cannot be updated post-creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this system setting was most recently modified.

Set automatically by backend upon any update (ISO 8601, UTC).

ITodoListSystemSetting.description:
Represents a single global configuration setting for the Todo List service.

Each entry defines an individual system-wide feature flag, operational threshold, or infrastructure parameter. Used by platform administrators to adjust runtime behavior, enable or disable global options, or document available settings. All relationships are internal; no foreign keys. Timestamps are managed by the backend for auditability and change tracking.

key.description:
Business-meaningful identifier for the global setting being created.

Represents the unique symbolic key for this system configuration entry (e.g., 'max_login_attempts', 'enable_signup'). System will reject attempts to create duplicate keys.

value.description:
String-encoded configuration value for this setting.

The backend will store values as string; application logic must interpret as needed (int, boolean, etc.). Field validation ensures maximum 1024 characters.

description.description:
Optional explanation, documentation, or operational context for this platform setting.

Used for service admin reference in the UI or operational documentation, not consumed by usual business logic.

ITodoListSystemSetting.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new global configuration setting for the Todo List system.

Used by privileged platform administrators to register a new system-wide configuration parameter, feature flag, or threshold. Key must be unique—duplicates trigger error. Description is optional and for admin/UIs only.

value.description:
New value (string-encoded) for the target configuration key.

This field is mandatory when updating a system setting. The value may be interpreted as int, boolean, etc. by business logic. Max length 1024 enforced.

description.description:
Optional updated explanation or doc-text for the setting.

Can be set to null or a new string to revise the admin-facing note for this setting. No effect on business logic.

ITodoListSystemSetting.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying the value or description of an existing global system setting by key.

Allows system administrators to update the string value (mandatory) and/or the explanation (optional) for any configuration setting. The setting key is in the path, not this body schema.

ITodoListSystemSetting.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a Todo List platform-wide system setting.

Used to display basic information about service-level configuration parameters, without including sensitive operational metadata. Typically used in lists or lookups of all current platform settings. Each summary includes the setting identity, value, and high-level documentation for clarity in administrative interfaces.

This is a lightweight variant that omits detailed audit or versioning fields, focusing on rapid reference for platform operators.

id.description: Unique identifier for the system setting (database primary key in UUID format).

key.description: Unique string identifier (business key) for the configuration parameter. Used as the authoritative name for retrieving or updating settings. E.g., 'max_login_attempts', 'enable_signup'.

value.description: String value assigned to this configuration setting. Interpreted by the backend for various platform options. Always stored as string regardless of intended application-level type.

description.description: Detailed administrative description or documentation for the setting. May be null if no explanation is provided. Used to clarify purpose, allowed values, defaults, or operational caveats for platform operators.

ITodoListSystemSetting.IRequest.description:
Query parameter body for filtering, sorting, and querying system settings in administrative APIs.

May specify key, time range, description, or sort order. All fields are optional, allowing maximum flexibility for administrator search/filter use cases. Used by PATCH /todoList/admin/systemSettings.

key.description: Filter by exact or partial (contains) setting key. If set, only records matching key (or substring) are returned.

description.description: Find settings containing this text in the description field. Enables full-text or partial search by context note, recommended for scenarios where operational or documentation context is known.

oneOf.description: Field by which to sort results. Use in conjunction with order. Allowed values: key, created_at, updated_at.
Field by which to sort results. Use in conjunction with order. Allowed values: key, created_at, updated_at.
Field by which to sort results. Use in conjunction with order. Allowed values: key, created_at, updated_at.

sort_by.description: Field by which to sort results. Use in conjunction with order. Allowed values: key, created_at, updated_at.

Direction to sort results. Allowed values: asc for ascending, desc for descending. Defaults to 'asc' if omitted.

order.description: Direction to sort results. Allowed values: asc for ascending, desc for descending. Defaults to 'asc' if omitted.

created_from.description: Filter settings created at or after this timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC).

created_to.description: Filter settings created at or before this timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC).

updated_from.description: Filter settings updated at or after this timestamp.

updated_to.description: Filter settings updated at or before this timestamp.

limit.description: Maximum record count per page (default 20, maximum 100).

ITodoListUser.description:
A registered end user in the Todo List system.

This schema represents a single user account as persisted in the todo_list_users Prisma model. It includes non-sensitive business and system fields such as email, account lock status, and timestamps, but intentionally omits sensitive password hash material and system authentication fields for security and privacy reasons.

This type is used in API responses where the full user entity must be exposed to the user (usually for their own information), supporting account/profile queries and updates. Account management is strictly private: only the user themselves can retrieve or modify their own record. All access and changes are subject to least-privilege and auditing policies.

id.description: User's unique identifier (UUID), assigned at account creation. Used as the primary key in the todo_list_users table.

email.description: User's unique login and contact email, used for communication, identity, and authentication. Must be unique for each user in the system.

is_locked.description: Account lock status. True if the user account is suspended or disabled due to abuse, compliance, or admin action. Locked users cannot login or perform actions.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when the user account was first created in the system.

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp of most recent account update (such as email change or lock status).

ITodoListUser.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for advanced search, filtering, and pagination of end user accounts in administrative API endpoints.

Allows platform admins to submit flexible queries against the todo_list_users table. Supported fields include partial email matches, account lock filter, date range filters, and pagination controls. This type mirrors admin search backend requirements and enables list APIs to efficiently filter and paginate large user datasets.

Sensitive data and password hashes are never accessible or queryable through this request DTO. Only platform admins may submit such queries in production. Rate limits and paging limits should be enforced in API usage.

email.description: Optional substring or full email address to filter users by partial match or exact search. Uses case-insensitive matching.

is_locked.description: Optional filter for account lock status. When true, only locked (suspended) users are included. When false, only unlocked (active) users.

created_at_from.description: Start of creation date range (inclusive, UTC). Only users created on or after this time are included.

created_at_to.description: End of creation date range (inclusive, UTC). Only users created on or before this time are included.

updated_at_from.description: Start of last update date range (inclusive, UTC). Only users updated on or after this time are included.

updated_at_to.description: End of last update date range (inclusive, UTC). Only users updated on or before this time are included.

page_size.description: Number of users per page (default: 20, max: 100).

oneOf.description: Sorting key for search results. Must be one of: created_at, updated_at, or email.
Sorting key for search results. Must be one of: created_at, updated_at, or email.
Sorting key for search results. Must be one of: created_at, updated_at, or email.

sort_by.description: Sorting key for search results. Must be one of: created_at, updated_at, or email.

oneOf.description: Result sort order. asc for ascending, desc for descending.
Result sort order. asc for ascending, desc for descending.

sort_order.description: Result sort order. asc for ascending, desc for descending.

email.description: New email address for the todo list user account. Must be globally unique. Changing the email updates the user's login and contact details. Value must follow standard RFC 5322 email format and application uniqueness constraints. Update is optional, and field is omitted if not changing email.

password.description: New plaintext password to set for the user account. Plain password will be hashed and stored per password security policies. If provided, must be at least 8 characters, subject to server-enforced validation (no common or easily guessed passwords, recommended use of letters, numbers, symbols). Leave undefined if password change is not desired.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating the authenticated user's todo list user account (todo_list_users).

May contain new email or password, or both, to update the currently authenticated user's own account. Fields are optional: at least one must be provided to effect any change. Only allows modifications to user-initiated fields—does not allow privilege elevation, account locking, or updates to system-managed fields. Updated_at is set automatically. Forbidden for any user to update another user's account.

Email and password fields are independently optional. If neither is provided or both are unchanged, the update has no effect. Email must be globally unique; password is only set if provided and meets security criteria. Account locking and ownership modifications are not permitted.

page.description: Page number for paginated session result set. Begins at 1 for the first page. Choose a reasonable value to retrieve more session records or browse a large user session history. Not required for unpaginated queries.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records to return in one page. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Used for efficient paging and large history review; defaults enforced by backend if omitted.

search.description: Optional text search keyword for filtering sessions by client metadata, IP address, or other session attributes. Enables quick narrowing to specific contexts. Typically matches partial IP, device, or origin information; behavior determined by server implementation.

oneOf.description: Session attribute to sort the results by. Choose either session creation time or expiration time, if sorting is supported by the backend. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'expired_at'. Not required unless the session review scenario calls for specific sorting.

Session attribute to sort the results by. Choose either session creation time or expiration time, if sorting is supported by the backend. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'expired_at'. Not required unless the session review scenario calls for specific sorting.

order_by.description: Session attribute to sort the results by. Choose either session creation time or expiration time, if sorting is supported by the backend. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'expired_at'. Not required unless the session review scenario calls for specific sorting.
